key_insight: The paper extends parameterized IQP generative quantum circuits from binary data to integer-valued data by reformulating the model with qudits to better preserve data structure.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more natural quantum machine learning encoding for non-binary engineering datasets, reducing information loss from forced binary mappings.
method: Encode each integer-valued pixel as a fixed-length bit-string.
Transform IQP gates into a qudit-compatible formalism.
Train the generative model with a custom loss function and covariance-based feature statistics.
evidence_signal: The approach is validated on electron shower energy-deposit data from the CLIC electromagnetic calorimeter, showing applicability to real high-energy physics measurements.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how integer values are discretized into fixed-length encodings, which can still introduce representational overhead and training complexity.
paper_title: Qudit extension of parameterized IQP circuits: A generative quantum machine learning approach to integer data
